June 15, 2026 
 
The Honorable Mehmet Oz, M.D. 
 Administrator 
 Centers for Medicare & Medicaid Services 
 U.S. Department of Health and Human Services 
 7500 Security Boulevard 
 Baltimore, MD 21244 
 
Re: CMS-0062-P â€“ Medicare and Medicaid Programs; Patient Protection and Affordable Care 
Act; Interoperability Standards and Prior Authorization for Drugs for Medicare Advantage 
Organizations, Medicaid Managed Care Plans, State Medicaid Agencies, Children's Health 
Insurance Program (CHIP) Agencies and CHIP Managed Care Entities, and Issuers of Qualified 
Health Plans on the Federally-Facilitated Exchanges 
 
Submitted electronically via regulations.gov 
athenahealth, Inc. ("athenahealth") appreciates the opportunity to respond to CMS-0062-P, the 
proposed rule addressing Interoperability Standards and Prior Authorization for Drugs across 
Medicare Advantage, Medicaid managed care, CHIP, and Qualified Health Plans on the Federally-
Facilitated Exchanges. 
For more than 29 years, athenahealth has supported clinicians caring for nearly one-fifth of the U.S. 
population across ambulatory and hospital settings in all 50 states. Our network includes more than 
170,000 providers, and our cloud-based athenaOne platform delivers electronic health record, 
practice management, care coordination, patient engagement, data analytics, and revenue cycle 
management capabilities that support clinical and operational workflows at scale. This position 
within the healthcare ecosystem provides us with direct visibility into how prior authorization 
policies are implemented in practice and where operational friction impacts care delivery. 
athenahealth's vision is to create a thriving healthcare ecosystem that delivers accessible, high 
quality, and sustainable healthcare for all. We work towards this vision partially by reducing 
burdensome administrative tasks for providers so that they can focus on improving patient 
outcomes. We believe that with the right engagement, there is an opportunity to streamline the prior 
authorization process and increase the ease of information sharing across the entire healthcare 
continuum. It is with that context that we offer the following comments. 
 
Electronic Prior Authorization for All Drugs: Building on Existing Infrastructure 
athenahealth supports CMS's proposal to expand the prior authorization API framework established 
in CMS-0057-F to support drugs covered under the medical benefit. Extending existing prior 
authorization API capabilities to these drugs will create a more consistent prior authorization 
experience across covered items, services, and therapies. 
athenahealth agrees that leveraging the standards-based framework established through prior CMS 
interoperability efforts can facilitate more efficient information exchange, support electronic 
documentation submission, and improve the timeliness of coverage determinations. Building upon 
existing infrastructure and implementation experience can simplify adoption for providers, health IT 
developers, and payers while supporting a more uniform approach across medical- and pharmacy-
 
benefit prior authorization. Providing comprehensive electronic prior authorization across medical 
services and drugs is an important step toward reducing the operational burden practices face when 
managing prior authorizations, simplifying implementation for health IT developers and plans, and 
improving the efficiency of prescribing workflows. 
Specific Reasons for Denials: Improving Transparency 
athenahealth supports CMSâ€™s proposal that impacted payers provide a specific reason when 
denying a prior authorization request for a drug. Clear and actionable denial information helps 
providers understand why a request was rejected and what steps are necessary for resubmission or 
appeal. This transparency will enable providers and staff to respond more efficiently and help reduce 
delays in patient care. 
If finalized, denial reasons for drugs should be communicated consistently across all automation 
channels. athenahealth recommends that CMS require denial reasons to be conveyed using 
standardized, machine-readable codes or categories wherever possible. Standardized denial 
reason codes would allow health IT systems to automate routing and follow-up activities, identify 
recurring denial trends, and support analytics that drive process improvements throughout the prior 
authorization lifecycle. 
Standardized Decision Timeframes: Promoting Predictability 
athenahealth supports CMSâ€™s proposal to establish maximum wait times for prior authorization 
decisions. Specifically, athenahealth supports the requirement that QHP issuers on the FFEs render 
decisions within 72 hours for standard requests and 24 hours for expedited requests, as well as the 
proposed 24-hour decision timeframe for prescription drugs in state CHIP FFS programs. 
Establishing clear and predictable decision timeframes can support better care management by 
setting consistent expectations for providers, patients, and payers. These requirements can also 
help reduce uncertainty in treatment planning and improve the overall prior authorization 
experience. 
API Endpoint Reporting: Improving Connectivity 
athenahealth supports CMSâ€™s proposal requiring payers to report their API endpoints and 
documentation URLs to CMS for centralized publication. Improving the discoverability of payer APIs 
will make it easier for developers and providers to identify, connect to, and maintain integrations 
with these systems. 
This proposal addresses a challenge experienced under CMS-0057-F, where establishing and 
maintaining connectivity between payers and health IT developers can be difficult and resource-
intensive.  
HIPAA Administrative Simplification: Advancing FHIR Adoption 
athenahealth supports CMSâ€™s proposal to adopt FHIR as the HIPAA standard for â€œreferral 
certification and authorizationâ€ and â€œeligibility for a health planâ€ transactions related to prior 
authorization, replacing the older X12N 278 standard. 
The future of electronic prior authorization is FHIR-based. Continued industry investment, 
implementation activity, and adoption trends demonstrate growing momentum behind FHIR-
enabled workflows. Adopting FHIR-based standards will help advance interoperability, support 
more modern data exchange capabilities, and establish a stronger foundation for future prior 
authorization innovation. 
 
Implementation Timeline: Aligning with Industry Readiness 
While athenahealth supports the objectives of CMS-0062-P, we remain concerned that the proposed 
October 1, 2027, implementation date does not provide sufficient time for stakeholders to 
successfully adopt the new requirements. 
Significant work is already underway across the industry to implement FHIR APIs for medical 
services pursuant to CMS-0057-F. However, the full impact of those APIs on provider workflows has 
not yet been realized. athenahealth therefore recommends that CMS establish a compliance date 
no earlier than January 1, 2029 for the drug-related prior authorization requirements. Providing 
additional implementation time would allow stakeholders to assess the effectiveness of the CMS-
0057-F infrastructure, incorporate lessons learned, and ensure that new requirements build upon a 
stable and mature foundation. This approach would increase the likelihood that expanding 
electronic prior authorization to drugs produces meaningful benefits for providers, payers, and 
patients. 
athenahealth appreciates the opportunity to provide comments on CMS-0062-P. We share CMSâ€™s 
commitment to advancing interoperability, reducing unnecessary administrative complexity, and 
supporting timely patient access to medically necessary treatments. We look forward to continuing 
to work with CMS, payers, providers, and other stakeholders to implement these proposals in a 
manner that delivers meaningful and lasting improvements across the healthcare ecosystem. 
Regards,  
  
Jennifer Michaels  
Senior Manager, Government & Regulatory Affairs   
athenahealth, Inc.
analysis:
## 1. COMMENTER INFORMATION

- **Author/Organization name:** athenahealth, Inc.; signed by Jennifer Michaels, Senior Manager, Government & Regulatory Affairs.
- **Stakeholder type:** Technology Vendor.
- **Credentials or expertise mentioned:** athenahealth states it has supported clinicians for more than 29 years, serves nearly one-fifth of the U.S. population, includes more than 170,000 providers, and offers the cloud-based athenaOne EHR, practice management, care coordination, patient engagement, analytics, and revenue cycle platform.

## 2. EXECUTIVE SUMMARY

athenahealth broadly supports CMS's drug prior authorization interoperability proposals, including expansion of the Prior Authorization API to medical benefit drugs, specific denial reasons, standardized decision timeframes, endpoint reporting, and adoption of FHIR as a HIPAA prior authorization standard. Its main modification request is to delay drug-related PA compliance until no earlier than January 1, 2029 so stakeholders can learn from CMS-0057-F implementation and build on a stable foundation.

## 3. REGULATORY CONTEXT

- **Specific provisions addressed:** PA-DRUG-MEDICAL; PA-DENIAL-REASONS; PA-TIMEFRAMES-DRUGS; API-ENDPOINT-REPORTING; HIPAA-PA-STANDARDS; IMPLEMENTATION-TIMELINE/GLOBAL timing considerations.
- **Regulatory citations mentioned:** No CFR sections cited by number; references CMS-0062-P and CMS-0057-F.
- **Standards referenced:** FHIR; FHIR APIs; X12N 278; standardized machine-readable denial reason codes/categories; API endpoint and documentation URLs.

## 4. DETAILED POSITIONS

**Topic 1: Electronic prior authorization for drugs under the medical benefit**
- **Provision ID:** PA-DRUG-MEDICAL
- **Position:** Support
- **Rationale:** athenahealth says extending the CMS-0057-F prior authorization API framework to medical benefit drugs will create a more consistent PA experience, improve information exchange, support electronic documentation, and reduce operational burden for providers, health IT developers, and payers.
- **Specific request:** Finalize the expansion while building on existing standards-based infrastructure and implementation experience.

**Topic 2: Specific denial reasons**
- **Provision ID:** PA-DENIAL-REASONS
- **Position:** Support/Modify
- **Rationale:** Clear denial reasons help providers understand rejections and take resubmission or appeal steps efficiently, reducing delays in care.
- **Specific request:** Require denial reasons to be communicated consistently across automation channels using standardized, machine-readable codes or categories wherever possible.

**Topic 3: Drug PA decision timeframes**
- **Provision ID:** PA-TIMEFRAMES-DRUGS
- **Position:** Support
- **Rationale:** Clear maximum wait times create predictable expectations and improve treatment planning and PA experience.
- **Specific request:** Finalize the 72-hour standard and 24-hour expedited FFE QHP timeframes and the 24-hour prescription drug timeframe for state CHIP FFS programs.

**Topic 4: API endpoint reporting**
- **Provision ID:** API-ENDPOINT-REPORTING
- **Position:** Support
- **Rationale:** Centralized publication of payer API endpoints and documentation URLs will improve discoverability and make developer-provider connectivity easier to establish and maintain.
- **Specific request:** Finalize payer endpoint and documentation URL reporting to CMS for centralized publication.

**Topic 5: FHIR as HIPAA prior authorization standard**
- **Provision ID:** HIPAA-PA-STANDARDS
- **Position:** Support
- **Rationale:** athenahealth states that the future of electronic prior authorization is FHIR-based and that adopting FHIR will advance interoperability, modern data exchange, and future PA innovation.
- **Specific request:** Adopt FHIR as the HIPAA standard for referral certification/authorization and eligibility transactions related to prior authorization, replacing X12N 278 for this context.

**Topic 6: Implementation timeline**
- **Provision ID:** PA-DRUG-MEDICAL; GENERAL
- **Position:** Modify
- **Rationale:** The commenter says the October 1, 2027 date does not give enough time to adopt new drug-related requirements, especially while CMS-0057-F FHIR API implementation is still underway and its provider workflow impacts are not yet fully known.
- **Specific request:** Establish a compliance date no earlier than January 1, 2029 for drug-related prior authorization requirements.

## 5. SOLICITATION RESPONSES

- **S12:** Supports using the existing prior authorization API framework for medical benefit drugs and suggests existing infrastructure can simplify adoption.
- **S16-S17:** Supports specific denial reasons and recommends standardized, machine-readable denial codes or categories.
- **S20/S43:** Supports maximum decision timeframes, including 72 hours standard and 24 hours expedited for QHP issuers, plus 24 hours for state CHIP FFS prescription drug requests.
- **S21:** Responds that the October 1, 2027 drug PA timeline is not achievable and recommends January 1, 2029 or later.
- **S23-S24/S33:** Supports centralized API endpoint and documentation URL reporting to improve connectivity and discoverability.
- **S44-S47/S50:** Supports FHIR as the HIPAA PA standard and replacing older X12N 278 for relevant prior authorization transactions, while linking implementation timing to industry readiness and CMS-0057-F lessons.

## 6. RECOMMENDATIONS

1. Finalize expansion of the prior authorization API framework to medical benefit drugs.
2. Require drug denial reasons to be clear, actionable, consistent across automation channels, and machine-readable where possible.
3. Finalize standardized maximum decision timeframes for QHP issuers and state CHIP FFS prescription drugs.
4. Require payers to report API endpoints and documentation URLs for centralized CMS publication.
5. Adopt FHIR as the HIPAA standard for prior authorization-related referral certification/authorization and eligibility transactions.
6. Set drug-related prior authorization compliance no earlier than January 1, 2029.
7. Use lessons from CMS-0057-F implementation before expanding requirements to drugs.

## 7. CONCERNS & OBJECTIONS

- **Primary concerns:** The October 1, 2027 implementation date is too soon; CMS-0057-F infrastructure and provider workflow impacts have not yet matured; denial reasons need standardization.
- **Potential negative impacts cited:** Premature implementation could reduce the chance that drug PA APIs produce meaningful benefits for providers, payers, and patients.
- **Implementation barriers mentioned:** Connectivity with payer APIs, resource-intensive integration maintenance, immature real-world CMS-0057-F experience, and lack of standardized machine-readable denial reasons.

## 8. SUPPORTING EVIDENCE

- **Data or statistics cited:** athenahealth states it supports clinicians caring for nearly one-fifth of the U.S. population and more than 170,000 providers.
- **Studies or research referenced:** None.
- **Examples provided:** Experience under CMS-0057-F shows that establishing and maintaining payer-health IT developer connectivity can be difficult and resource-intensive.

## 9. IMPACT ASSESSMENT

- **Affected stakeholders:** Providers, patients, payers, QHP issuers, state CHIP FFS programs, health IT developers, API developers, and EHR/practice management vendors.
- **Economic implications:** The comment implies that standardized APIs, endpoint reporting, and machine-readable denial reasons can reduce administrative burden and integration costs, while rushed timelines may increase implementation expense.
- **Technical feasibility:** athenahealth considers FHIR-based electronic PA technically appropriate but says the industry needs more time to mature CMS-0057-F infrastructure and apply lessons learned.
- **Patient care impact:** More efficient PA, transparent denial reasons, and predictable timeframes could reduce treatment delays and improve prescribing workflows.

## 10. SENTIMENT ANALYSIS

- **Overall position:** Supportive with timeline concerns
- **Tone:** Professional, technical, and collaborative
- **Priority level:** High

## 11. KEY QUOTES

1. "athenahealth supports CMS's proposal to expand the prior authorization API framework" - Context: Indicates support for PA-DRUG-MEDICAL.
2. "denial reasons for drugs should be communicated consistently across all automation channels" - Context: Supports standardized machine-readable denial reasons.
3. "The future of electronic prior authorization is FHIR-based" - Context: Supports HIPAA-PA-STANDARDS.
4. "compliance date no earlier than January 1, 2029" - Context: States the main requested timeline modification.

## 12. THEMES

- [x] **IMPLEMENTATION-TIMELINE** - athenahealth requests delaying compliance from October 1, 2027 to no earlier than January 1, 2029.
- [x] **PROVIDER-BURDEN** - The comment repeatedly frames electronic PA as a way to reduce administrative workload for providers and staff.
- [x] **TECHNICAL-FEASIBILITY** - It discusses FHIR APIs, endpoint discoverability, connectivity, and implementation readiness.
- [x] **STANDARDS-MATURITY** - The comment supports FHIR but asks CMS to let CMS-0057-F experience mature before drug PA expansion.
- [x] **PATIENT-ACCESS** - Faster, more predictable PA and clear denial reasons are tied to avoiding delays in patient care.
- [x] **STAKEHOLDER-COORDINATION** - The comment highlights implementation across CMS, payers, providers, health IT developers, and other stakeholders.
- [x] **TRANSPARENCY** - It supports specific denial reasons and centralized publication of payer API endpoints.
- [x] **EXISTING-WORKFLOWS** - The commenter focuses on provider prescribing workflows, automated routing, follow-up, and integration maintenance.
- [x] **VENDOR-ECOSYSTEM** - athenahealth writes from the health IT developer perspective and emphasizes API integration and developer readiness.
